content: Chlorpheniramine is an antihistamine that is prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as red, itchy, watery eyes, sneezing, and a runny nose caused by allergies, hay fever, or the common cold. It can also be used to relieve itching from insect bites, bee stings, poison ivy, and poison oak. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in various forms, including extended-release tablets and capsules, regular tablets and capsules, chewable tablets, liquid, and syrup, all of which are taken orally. It is typically taken every 4 to 6 hours or twice daily, in the morning and evening, as needed. You should follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. It is crucial to take chlorpheniramine exactly as directed and not to take more or less than prescribed. Extended-release tablets and capsules should not be broken, crushed, or chewed, and they must be swallowed whole. Children under 12 years of age should not be given extended-release forms, and children under 6 years of age should not be given regular or chewable tablets or liquid forms unless specifically directed by a doctor. Before taking chlorpheniramine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially those for colds, hay fever, allergies, depression, seizures, muscle relaxation, pain relief (narcotics), sedation, sleep aids, tranquilizers, or vitamins. Do not take chlorpheniramine if you have used an MAO inhibitor in the past two weeks. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, notify your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking chlorpheniramine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the sedative effects of this drug, so it should be avoided. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Chlorpheniramine may cause side effects. Minor side effects include dry mouth, nose, and throat; upset stomach; headache; chest congestion; and diarrhea. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include vision problems, difficulty urinating, difficulty breathing, muscle weakness, prolonged drowsiness, excitement (especially in children), dizziness, and skin rash. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while taking this medication. Do not share it with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Chlorpheniramine is available under various brand names, including Aller-Chlor®, Chlor-Trimeton®, Polaramine®, and others. It is also included in combination products such as Alka-Seltzer Plus® Cold Medicine Liqui-Gels®, Coricidin® HBP® Cold & Flu, and Tylenol® Allergy Sinus Maximum Strength, among many others.
